title: Henselian rigidity for w-contractible lisse condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_T[0]$, and $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of dualizable objects (objects admitting evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities). For a profinite set $S$, use the analogous notation for sheaves on profinite sets over $S$, with finite jointly surjective covering families and coefficient ring the restriction of $\Lambda$ to that site. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, with the closed immersion $i:Z\to T$. Then $\pi_0(Z)\to\pi_0(T)$ is a homeomorphism, and $T$ is w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal] if and only if $Z$ is w-contractible. When these conditions hold, the exact symmetric monoidal inverse image induces an equivalence
$$i^*:D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\mathrm{lis}}(Z,\Lambda).$$
In particular it is fully faithful on morphisms between dualizable objects. The coefficient identification $i^*\Lambda_T\cong\Lambda_Z$ is the canonical one, so $i^*$ commutes with the scalar extension of constant discrete complexes.

proof.text: Apply Algebra.existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_of_henselianRing from [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-integral-idempotent-lifting] to the integral A-algebra A. Rewrite I.map (algebraMap A A) = I. The equivalences PrimeSpectrum.isIdempotentElemEquivClopens from [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] identify inverse image of D(e) with D(q(e)). Unique lifting gives injectivity and existence gives surjectivity of clopen inverse image.

proof.text: The affine schemes $T,Z$ have spectral underlying spaces by [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Step 1 and [lem-sfb-spectral-clopen-component-homeomorphism], applied to $i$, give the homeomorphism $h=\pi_0(i):Q=\pi_0(Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}P=\pi_0(T)$.

proof.text: By [lem-zl-henselian-wstrict-local-invariance], $A$ is w-strictly local exactly when $A/I$ is. By Step 2, $P$ is extremally disconnected exactly when $Q$ is: a homeomorphism preserves open sets, their closures, and openness of those closures. The definition [sk-def-pe-wlocal] of w-contractibility is the conjunction of these two conditions, so $T$ is w-contractible if and only if $Z$ is.

Assume w-contractibility of A and A/I. Transport it to the global section rings of their spectra along Scheme.ΓSpecIso. Take the coherent component System from [lem-zl-component-derived-pullback-square]. Apply [lem-zl-condensed-component-pullback-compatibility] with each Corner's own continuity, braided and exact instances, obtaining a component lisse equivalence with coefficient isomorphism alpha. Compare alpha with that Corner's coefficient isomorphism c: restriction of scalars along the ring automorphism c^{-1} followed by alpha is an exact monoidal equivalence. Mod.comapCongr and Mod.comapComp identify the Corner module functor with componentModules(alpha) followed by that scalar equivalence. Termwise derived comparison and restriction to the full subcategories of dualizable objects therefore give lisse equivalences for the two actual Corners. The generic monoidal-equivalence restriction is proved by transporting duals in both directions. [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality] supplies the prescribed exact symmetric monoidal scheme pullback.

Use Square.theta from [lem-zl-component-derived-pullback-square]: the actual Corner derived pullback followed by the scheme pullback is naturally isomorphic to the actual slice derived pullback followed by the other Corner. Lift this natural isomorphism through the fully faithful inclusions of dualizable objects, using the preservation statements in the System. No new comparison map is chosen.

source.place: Corollary 4.4(2), final sentence, with the construction (4.1) preceding Proposition 4.3

proof.text: The homeomorphism on components makes affineComponentMap(i) an isomorphism in Profinite. Over.pullback along it and its inverse compose to identity by Over.pullbackComp and Over.pullbackId. Applying continuous sheaf pushforward gives an equivalence of slice direct images; the slice adjunction gives an equivalence of inverse images. The induced functor on internal modules is an equivalence: its adjunction unit and counit are isomorphisms on underlying sheaves, and the forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. Coefficient restriction and termwise derivation preserve this equivalence. The System's monoidal structure restricts it to dualizable objects. In the restricted square, both Corner functors and the slice functor are equivalences; transport across theta and cancel the source Corner to prove the actual restricted scheme pullback is an equivalence. Its inclusion comparison is reflexive, since the restricted functor is constructed by ObjectProperty.lift. The already constructed discreteScalarExtensionPullbackIso records the canonical scalar compatibility.
